limitations: Physical phones, Safari/Firefox, real Wi-Fi latency and modest physical-device performance were not certified; mobile tests used Chromium touch emulation and LAN used two browser clients on one host.

Full maze and shooter proofs use controlled clocks and synthetic DOM events; the runner campaign uses native keyboard input with a controlled browser clock. Native real-time input checks are separate and documented. No full-campaign wall-clock audio synchronization or human audio audition is claimed.
These are original evocations at documented campaign scale. Exact proprietary formulas, original wave/level geometry, historical roster, art and music parity are not claimed.

Offline verification bundles Linux x86_64 Chrome Headless Shell and JavaScript dependencies; Node 22.18+ and standard Chromium system libraries are prerequisites. Other operating-system verification runtimes are not bundled.
Deadlock LAN requires the included Node host and an open authority tab, supports two players, and has no host migration. Same-phone local co-op touch controls are not claimed.

The existing Work container/home and network policy were reused. Browser setup required adaptation; some successful untouched-baseline play occurred after initial source edits, as disclosed in the relevant records.

The native generation agent was interrupted after producing the release and completed packaged gate but before locking. The operator finalized metadata, evidence and delivery without changing the game code. Exact model/effort identifiers were not exposed; defaults were not overridden.
